code:
(λx.λy.x) y
->β  [x := y] (λy.x)    # naively substitute y for x
->β  λy.y               # WRONG: the free y is now captured by λy!
description: You can see how naive substitution changes a free variable into a bound variable.

steps.description: The argument y is free. The function's inner lambda also uses y as its parameter name.
The written substitution replaces x with y inside the inner lambda.

steps.answer: The inner lambda y binds it, capturing the argument's formerly free y.
steps.question: In the written result lambda y.y, which binder controls the final y?

steps.description: The annotation marks this derivation as wrong because it produces identity. The supplied evaluator output instead keeps the argument y free by renaming the binder.

title: Spot variable capture
